The derivative of ${e}^{x}$ is just ${e}^{x}$ itself. On the other hand, $ln⁡8$ is a constant, so its derivative is $0.$

Using the addition rule, then, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6{e}^{x}+ln⁡8) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6{e}^{x})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡8) \\  & =6\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x})+0 \\  & =6{e}^{x}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
